intro.title: Deployment strategies
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn about different deployment strategies used to release software updates safely and reliably. You will explore concepts like blue-green deployments, canary releases, and rolling updates, understanding how each minimizes downtime and risk. The core focus is on the operational patterns and decision-making involved in choosing a strategy. You will apply these concepts through hands-on exercises that simulate deployment scenarios, using common production engineering tools and workflows.
intro.usecase: Deployment strategies are essential for ensuring reliable software updates in production environments. They enable engineering teams to release new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements with minimal user disruption. For example, blue-green deployments allow instant rollback if issues arise, while canary releases gradually expose changes to a small user subset before full rollout. These strategies are commonly implemented in CI/CD pipelines for web applications, mobile apps, and cloud services to maintain high availability and reduce deployment risks.
